title: Skewer Party!
summary: Draw the rook onto e6 so forcing queen checks can line up the king and undefended queen.

nodes.question: How can White answer the attack on Qf1?
nodes.explanation: After ...Rxf6, White has Kb4, Re2 and Qf1 against Kc6, Rf6 and Qg7. Re6+ diverts the rook before the queen begins its checking route.

branches.title: Skewer along the seventh rank
commentary: Begin after ...Rxf6 at three seconds in the complete six-piece position. The preceding rook capture is source context.
Re6+ checks Kc6 while offering the rook and attacking Rf6. Black must answer the check instead of simply taking Qf1.
Rxe6 accepts the rook, placing it one square farther from White’s queen-checking route.
Qa6+ begins the precise checking sequence.
Kd7 is the illustrated upper king retreat.
Qb7+ checks along the seventh rank, skewering the king against the undefended Qg7.
Kd6 steps away from the checking rank.
Qxg7 wins the queen. The exact queen-versus-rook endpoint is won; further conversion is outside this selected line.
branches.explanation: Qxg7 wins the queen. The exact queen-versus-rook endpoint is won; further conversion is outside this selected line.

branches.title: Skewer along the long diagonal
commentary: Compare the source’s lower king route after the same rook deflection.
Re6+ checks the king and offers the last rook to move the defender away from f6.
Rxe6 accepts the sacrifice.
Qa6+ starts the queen pursuit.
Kd5 avoids the immediate seventh-rank skewer.
Qc4+ checks and forces a further king decision.
Ke5 is the illustrated retreat onto the c3–g7 diagonal.
Qc3+ checks along that diagonal and skewers the king against Qg7. Moving Rf6 to e6 cleared this line.
Kf5 leaves the diagonal, as shown in the saved board.
Qxg7 captures the queen and reaches an exactly checked queen-versus-rook win.

branches.title: The king backtracks toward d6
commentary: Compare the source’s backtracking king route rather than ...Ke5.
Re6+ offers the rook with check to deflect the defender.
Rxe6 accepts the sacrifice.
Qa6+ checks from the sixth rank.
Kd5 avoids the upper skewer for now.
Qc4+ checks and forces the king to choose again.
Kd6 backtracks instead of entering the diagonal skewer.
Qc5+ drives the king upward while keeping the black queen undefended.
Kd7 reaches the source’s next checking alignment.
Qa7+ skewers Kd7 against Qg7 along the seventh rank. The checked position is winning; the line stops at the skewer without inventing another king reply.

exercises.prompt: Why sacrifice the rook on e6?
exercises.answer: The capture moves Black’s rook off f6. In the ...Ke5 branch, that clears the diagonal from c3 through e5 and f6 to Qg7, enabling the skewer.

exercises.prompt: What do the forcing checks accomplish?
exercises.answer: They make the king choose between routes that align it with the undefended queen. The lesson compares selected source defenses rather than claiming to enumerate every legal move.

startContext: Begin after ...Rxf6 at three seconds, in a visually reconstructed six-piece board. The preceding seven-piece capture is source context. Three selected source routes after Re6 ...Rxe6 compare the upper, diagonal and backtracking skewers. Every encoded position is checked exactly; a queen-versus-rook win is distinguished from an immediate mate.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
